decision: Decide whether TensorLBM may (D1) adopt MF-LBM's iso8 wall-normal table as its curved/voxel wall-orientation preprocessor, or (D2) keep a local alternative (raw central differences / no table).
alternatives: D1 iso8 isotropic gradient of a 4x D3Q27-smoothed solid fraction (OSS) transplanted into TensorLBM
D2 2nd-order central differences of the same smoothed indicator
D3 no smoothing (raw staircase indicator) with either stencil
hypothesis: H1: the transplant is semantics-exact against the OSS binary (<=1e-12 max |dn|). H2: with 4 smoothing iterations the iso8 table reproduces analytic wall normals on a curved staircase within the owner 15% band (mean chordal relative error), and beats raw/central alternatives.

metrics.K1_exactness: max_abs_dn = max |n_ours - n_OSS| over the identical node table; also node-set identity and la_weight identity
metrics.K2_accuracy: mean and max chordal relative normal error 2 sin(dtheta/2) against the analytic normal (sphere radial / plane normal); owner band 15%
metrics.K3_isotropy: max/min directional gain of the operator on analytic linear fields (1.0 = isotropic)
metrics.K4_curvature: mean kappa = -div(n) over the +/-1 cell band around the analytic level set vs 2/R (sphere); relative error

unit_of_analysis: one geometry x stencil arm; KPIs are per-node normal errors aggregated to mean/max/p95

baseline_control.physical: analytic normals (sphere radial direction, plane normal) - exact reference, no numerical baseline needed
baseline_control.representation_control: same smoothed indicator field fed to iso8 vs 2nd-order central differences, so the only changed variable is the stencil
baseline_control.oss_note: the OSS arm is not a re-implementation: the upstream Fortran preprocessor is compiled with gfortran and run on the byte-identical wall array, then the binary normal table is parsed and compared row by row

predeclared_thresholds.interpretation: K1 is a semantics-identity check, hence machine-precision; K2/K4 use the owner 15% band; a mean inside the band with individual nodes outside is reported as such (no trimming).

stopping_rule: every arm is run to completion on a fixed geometry list (n=48/64 sphere, n=40 plane at 26.565 and 45 deg); no case is added or dropped after seeing KPIs; wall clock budget 900 s per arm (all arms ran in <1 s of solver time, 37 s total including the OSS build).
variables_held_fixed: voxelised wall array (identical bytes for both arms)
confounders: upstream leaves mirror_bc unset (undefined); the harness builds with -finit-integer=0 so the arm is deterministic - a real upstream defect, recorded as D7 in the difference list
the OSS preprocessor lists nodes in the 4-cell overlap band outside the physical box; the analytic comparison is restricted to physical nodes (K1 is computed on the full table)
individual staircase nodes near the 45 deg corners carry an O(1) local error in any gradient stencil; the mean is the acceptance quantity and the max is reported untrimmed
analysis: grouped by geometry and arm, no outlier removal, errors vs analytic; sensitivity = smoothing sweep + resolution change; exactness compared elementwise against the OSS binary table
fail_stage_plan: fail_stage in {stencil_parse, oss_build, oss_run, table_build, comparison, curvature}; failure_reason carries the measured deviation

amendments.what: curvature metric fixed as kappa = -div(n) after the sign convention was measured (grad points into the solid, so the sphere's inward normal field has divergence -2/R)
amendments.why: first pass compared div(n) directly with +2/R and reported a 180%-looking error that was purely a sign convention, not a solver deviation
